questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Epithelia: layers, shape and function
questions.prompt: A lining has nuclei at different heights. What additional observation best distinguishes pseudostratified from stratified epithelium?

options.text: Trace whether every cell reaches the basement membrane.
options.explanation: In pseudostratified epithelium all cells reach the basement membrane, although some do not reach the lumen; true stratification includes cells above the basal layer.

options.text: Count all nuclei seen in the section, regardless of cell boundaries.
options.explanation: Nuclear height or the total number of nuclear profiles alone cannot establish the number of epithelial layers.

options.text: Check whether the superficial cells are taller than they are wide.
options.explanation: Surface-cell shape helps name an epithelium, but columnar cells can occur in both arrangements.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Epithelia: layers, shape and function
questions.prompt: A model exchange surface changes from one thin cell layer to several layers. With other variables fixed, what is the most direct consequence?

options.text: Diffusion becomes faster because there are more cells.
options.explanation: Adding layers increases the diffusion path; cell number alone does not improve passive exchange.

options.text: The diffusion path increases, making passive exchange slower.
options.explanation: A thin barrier shortens the path for diffusion. Several layers may help resist abrasion but impose a longer exchange path.

options.text: Transport is unchanged as long as the surface area is unchanged.
options.explanation: Diffusion depends on barrier thickness as well as area and the concentration or partial-pressure gradient.

questions.subject: biochemistry
questions.title: Amino-acid nitrogen and urea
questions.prompt: Why can transferring an amino group to glutamate not, by itself, complete nitrogen disposal?

options.text: The nitrogen has changed carrier but still needs a route to elimination.
options.explanation: Transamination redistributes nitrogen. The amino nitrogen must still be processed and ultimately excreted; the carbon skeleton follows its own metabolic fate.

options.text: Transamination always converts the amino nitrogen directly into urea.
options.explanation: Urea formation requires the urea-cycle reactions. An amino-group transfer is not the complete disposal pathway.

options.text: Once nitrogen reaches glutamate it cannot enter another pathway.
options.explanation: Glutamate collects and transfers nitrogen; it is a metabolic intermediate rather than a permanent endpoint.

questions.subject: physiology
questions.title: Predict a renal circuit response
questions.prompt: In the fixed-pressure two-resistor model, double efferent resistance while keeping afferent resistance at 1. What happens relative to baseline?

options.text: Flow falls and glomerular pressure rises.
options.explanation: Total resistance increases, lowering flow. A larger share of the fixed pressure drop is across the efferent resistance, raising pressure upstream of it. This circuit does not calculate GFR.

options.text: Flow and glomerular pressure both fall.
options.explanation: Flow falls, but efferent resistance is downstream of the glomerular node; pressure at that node rises in this fixed-pressure model.

options.text: Flow rises because glomerular pressure rises.
options.explanation: Pressure at an intermediate point is not the same as flow through the circuit. Total resistance has increased.

questions.subject: physiology
questions.title: Predict a renal circuit response
questions.prompt: Now double only afferent resistance. Which prediction follows from the same model?

options.text: Flow falls but glomerular pressure rises.
options.explanation: That was the downstream-resistance manipulation. Increasing upstream resistance lowers pressure at the glomerular node.

options.text: Flow and glomerular pressure both fall.
options.explanation: The total resistance rises and more of the pressure drop occurs before the glomerular node. This is a circuit prediction, not a clinical GFR estimate.

options.text: Flow is unchanged because arterial pressure is fixed.
options.explanation: A fixed driving pressure does not fix flow when total resistance changes.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Real section A
questions.prompt: Which classification best describes the lining of the large open tubule in section A?

options.text: Simple cuboidal epithelium
options.explanation: The lining forms one layer of cells with roughly similar height and width. Follow a single tubule wall; nearby tubules are separate structures, not extra epithelial layers.

options.text: Stratified cuboidal epithelium
options.explanation: Several adjacent tubules can mimic layers. A stratified epithelium has multiple layers within one lining between its basal boundary and free surface.

options.text: Simple squamous epithelium
options.explanation: Squamous cells are flattened. These tubular cells have appreciable cytoplasm around rounded nuclear profiles.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Transfer section B
questions.prompt: How should the thick lining facing the broad pale space in section B be classified?

options.text: Simple columnar epithelium
options.explanation: One layer of tall cells would connect the basal boundary to the surface. This lining contains many cell layers.

options.text: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium
options.explanation: Uneven nuclear heights alone do not make an epithelium stratified. Here the tissue has distinct stacked layers with flattening toward the free surface.

options.text: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.explanation: Multiple layers lie between the basal boundary and the free surface. Superficial cells flatten, so classification uses the surface cells rather than the deeper rounded cells.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.title: Volume V: trace a limb nerve through the plexus
questions.prompt: In a simplified plexus map, trace a C5 fibre into the axillary nerve. Which route fits?

options.text: Upper trunk → posterior division → posterior cord
options.explanation: C5 contributes to the upper trunk; its posterior division contributes to the posterior cord, from which the axillary nerve arises.

options.text: Upper trunk → anterior division → lateral cord
options.explanation: The upper trunk is correct, but its anterior division contributes to the lateral cord, not the cord giving rise to the axillary nerve.

options.text: Lower trunk → posterior division → posterior cord
options.explanation: The cord fits, but the usual lower trunk combines C8–T1 rather than C5.

questions.subject: anatomy
questions.title: Volume V: trace a limb nerve through the plexus
questions.prompt: A model shows the three cords beside an artery deep to pectoralis minor. What identifies the landmark used to name the cords?

options.text: The axillary artery before it reaches pectoralis minor
options.explanation: That is the first part. Cord names refer to their relations to the second part.

options.text: The second part of the axillary artery
options.explanation: Pectoralis minor divides the artery into parts; the second part lies deep to the muscle and defines the cord names.

options.text: The brachial artery below teres major
options.explanation: This is distal to the axillary artery and is not the landmark defining the cord names.

questions.title: Histology Foundations: The Four Basic Tissues
questions.subject: histology
questions.prompt: A superficial injury removes an epithelial lining while deeper smooth muscle remains intact. Which immediate functional loss follows most directly from the tissue that was removed?

options.text: All active force generation in the deeper muscle is abolished
options.explanation: The scenario preserves the deeper muscle. Loss of epithelial cells does not by itself establish loss of all muscle contraction.

options.text: The continuous protective barrier is disrupted
options.explanation: Epithelial continuity and cell junctions help maintain a barrier. Removing the lining exposes underlying tissue even when deeper contractile cells remain.

options.text: The extracellular collagen necessarily disappears from the supporting tissue
options.explanation: Collagen belongs to the supporting matrix. Its disappearance is not implied by selective removal of the epithelial layer.

questions.title: Histology Foundations: The Four Basic Tissues
questions.subject: histology
questions.prompt: An unknown pink bundle has sparse flattened nuclei between abundant parallel extracellular fibres. No striations are seen. Which interpretation is best supported?

options.text: Dense regular connective tissue, because matrix dominates over cells
options.explanation: Abundant aligned extracellular collagen with relatively sparse flattened fibroblast nuclei supports dense regular connective tissue such as tendon. This uses positive architectural clues.

options.text: Smooth muscle, because absent striations identify a non-striated contractile bundle
options.explanation: Absent striations are not specific to smooth muscle. The positive findings here are abundant extracellular fibres and sparse flattened nuclei, which favour dense regular connective tissue.

options.text: Skeletal muscle cut obliquely, because orientation can conceal its striations
options.explanation: An oblique cut can obscure striations, but it does not explain a field dominated by extracellular collagen with sparse flattened nuclei. The stated architecture supports connective tissue.

questions.title: Histology Foundations: The Four Basic Tissues
questions.subject: histology
questions.prompt: Selective myelin injury affects a peripheral nerve while its axons initially remain intact. Which functional prediction and glial-cell attribution are best supported?

options.text: Conduction may slow or fail, and the affected myelin was formed by oligodendrocytes
options.explanation: The functional prediction is plausible, but the cell attribution is incorrect. Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin; the question specifies a peripheral nerve.

options.text: Conduction must remain normal because the axons are still present
options.explanation: Axonal continuity does not guarantee normal conduction. Damage to insulating myelin can impair action-potential propagation even while the axon is initially intact.

options.text: Conduction may slow or fail, and the affected myelin was formed by Schwann cells
options.explanation: PNS myelin comes from Schwann cells and supports efficient action-potential propagation. This predicts a functional disturbance without assuming the whole neuron has died.

questions.title: Anatomy Foundations: Position, Planes and Organisation
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.prompt: A hypothetical teaching image is a transverse section viewed from the feet towards the head, with anterior at the top. A marker is in the upper-left part of the display. Which description follows from this orientation?

options.text: Patient’s left and posterior
options.explanation: This reverses both supplied orientation cues. The patient’s left appears on the display’s right, and posterior is at the bottom.

options.text: Patient’s right and anterior
options.explanation: Under the stated viewing convention, display-left corresponds to the patient’s right. The top of this image is explicitly labelled anterior.

options.text: Patient’s right and superior within the section
options.explanation: The patient’s side is correct, but superior is perpendicular to a transverse section. The top of this display is anterior, not superior.

questions.title: Anatomy Foundations: Position, Planes and Organisation
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.prompt: A hypothetical report describes fluid between the right visceral and parietal pleura. Which interpretation is anatomically justified?

options.text: Fluid is inside the right main bronchus
options.explanation: A bronchial lumen is within an airway. The report specifies a space outside the lung surface between pleural layers.

options.text: Fluid is in the pericardial cavity
options.explanation: The pericardial cavity is between serous pericardial layers, not pleural layers. The report identifies different boundaries.

options.text: Fluid occupies the right pleural cavity
options.explanation: The two named pleural surfaces define this space. This locates the fluid without establishing its cause or prescribing treatment.

questions.title: Anatomy Foundations: Position, Planes and Organisation
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.prompt: A hypothetical superficial mark lies on the anterior right forearm, closer to the wrist than to the elbow. Which statement remains justified when the person turns the palm down?

options.text: The mark remains on the anatomical anterior surface of the right forearm
options.explanation: Rotating the limb changes its displayed orientation, not the established anatomical name of its surface or its side.

options.text: The mark becomes posterior because it now faces away from the viewer
options.explanation: The viewer’s changing position cannot rename anatomical surfaces. Use the reference position to describe the mark consistently.

options.text: The mark proves an underlying nerve injury
options.explanation: Surface location alone does not establish damage to a deep nerve. Depth, function and additional observations would be needed.

questions.title: Anatomy Foundations: Position, Planes and Organisation
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.prompt: In a simplified stomach-wall model, the epithelial lining remains intact while smooth-muscle contraction is reduced. Which function is most directly affected by the specified change?

options.text: The ability of the lining to form an epithelial barrier must be completely lost
options.explanation: Reduced muscle contraction does not itself establish epithelial destruction. The stem explicitly preserves the lining.

options.text: Mechanical mixing of the luminal contents
options.explanation: Smooth-muscle contraction contributes to mixing and propulsion. This prediction follows from the affected tissue’s function without assuming that every tissue has failed.

options.text: Chemical secretion by the intact epithelial lining is the function most directly reduced.
options.explanation: The lining is stated to remain intact; reduced smooth-muscle contraction most directly affects mechanical mixing and propulsion, although tissue functions can interact.

questions.title: Physiology Foundations: Membrane Transport and Resting Potential
questions.subject: physiology
questions.prompt: In a teaching model, the Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase is inhibited while Na⁺ leaks continue. After the Na⁺ gradient weakens, what happens to the energy available for Na⁺-coupled glucose uptake?

options.text: It increases because the cotransporter starts hydrolysing ATP.
options.explanation: The cotransporter does not become an ATPase when the separate pump is inhibited.

options.text: It is unchanged because a protein transporter needs no gradient.
options.explanation: Secondary active transport depends on the coupled electrochemical gradient, not simply the presence of a protein.

options.text: It decreases because the downhill Na⁺ movement supplies less energy.
options.explanation: Weakening the Na⁺ electrochemical gradient reduces the driving force available to support uphill glucose transport.

questions.title: Physiology Foundations: Membrane Transport and Resting Potential
questions.subject: physiology
questions.prompt: A model membrane is permeable only to K⁺. Intracellular K⁺ stays fixed while extracellular K⁺ increases but remains below the intracellular concentration. What happens to the K⁺ equilibrium potential?

options.text: It becomes more negative.
options.explanation: Raising outside K⁺ reduces the outward concentration gradient; less negative voltage is needed to oppose it.

options.text: It becomes less negative.
options.explanation: The outside-to-inside K⁺ concentration ratio increases, shifting the K⁺ equilibrium potential in the positive direction.

options.text: It is unchanged because K⁺ is not actively transported through the channel.
options.explanation: The equilibrium potential depends on the concentration ratio even though movement through the channel is passive.

questions.title: Biochemistry Foundations: Enzymes, Kinetics and Regulation
questions.subject: biochemistry
questions.prompt: Under ideal reversible competitive inhibition, the active enzyme amount and other conditions stay fixed. Which pattern is predicted?

options.text: Higher apparent Km with unchanged Vmax.
options.explanation: More substrate is needed for half the limiting rate, but sufficient substrate can still approach the same Vmax.

options.text: Lower Vmax with unchanged apparent Km in every case.
options.explanation: This is the ideal pure non-competitive pattern, not the competitive model specified in the question.

options.text: Lower apparent Km with higher Vmax.
options.explanation: Competition does not increase catalytic capacity or reduce the substrate requirement in this model.

questions.title: Biochemistry Foundations: Enzymes, Kinetics and Regulation
questions.subject: biochemistry
questions.prompt: A hypothetical Michaelis–Menten assay has Vmax = 60 µmol/min and Km = 3 mmol/L. At [S] = 3 mmol/L, what is the initial rate?

options.text: 60 µmol/min
options.explanation: Vmax is the limiting rate approached at high substrate, not the rate when [S] equals Km.

options.text: 30 mmol/L
options.explanation: The numerical half is correct, but this is a concentration unit rather than a rate.

options.text: 30 µmol/min
options.explanation: At [S] = Km, v = Vmax/2 = 30 µmol/min; the answer must retain rate units.

questions.title: Genetics Foundations: Genome, Inheritance and Gene Expression
questions.subject: genetics
questions.prompt: In an Aa × Aa autosomal recessive cross, assume AA and Aa are unaffected and aa is affected. Before knowing the phenotype, what is the probability of an Aa carrier child?

options.explanation: One of the four combinations is AA and one is aa, but two are heterozygous carriers.
Aa and aA are the two heterozygous outcomes among four equally likely combinations, giving 1/2.

options.text: Two thirds
options.explanation: Two thirds is the carrier probability conditional on an unaffected child in this model. That condition has not been supplied.

questions.title: Genetics Foundations: Genome, Inheritance and Gene Expression
questions.subject: genetics
questions.prompt: Two cell types contain the same intact gene, but one has much less of its mRNA. Which conclusion is justified by these observations alone?

options.text: RNA abundance differs; the gene need not be absent from either cell.
options.explanation: Different transcription or RNA stability can change mRNA abundance even when the DNA sequence is present in both cells.

options.text: The cell with less mRNA must have lost the chromosome.
options.explanation: The question states that the same intact gene is present; mRNA abundance alone does not show chromosome loss.

options.text: Both cells must contain equal amounts of functional protein.
options.explanation: DNA presence does not fix RNA or protein abundance, and function also depends on later processing and regulation.

questions.title: Biophysics Foundations: Diffusion, Osmosis and Membranes
questions.subject: biophysics
questions.prompt: Two compartments have equal initial hydrostatic pressure. A membrane passes water but not the dissolved solute. The right side has more solute particles per litre. What is the initial net water movement?

options.text: From right to left
options.explanation: That direction would increase the initial osmotic imbalance under the stated equal-pressure conditions.

options.text: No net movement because solute cannot cross
options.explanation: Solute impermeability does not prevent water movement; the membrane is explicitly permeable to water.

options.text: From left to right
options.explanation: Water initially moves towards the more concentrated impermeant-solute compartment when initial hydrostatic pressures are equal.

questions.title: Biophysics Foundations: Diffusion, Osmosis and Membranes
questions.subject: biophysics
questions.prompt: A model cell and bath initially have equal total osmolarity. The bath solute can enter the cell. Is unchanged cell volume guaranteed over time?

options.text: Yes, equal osmolarity always means equal tonicity.
options.explanation: Equal total particle concentration does not account for solute permeability or redistribution over time.

options.text: No; solute permeability and redistribution must also be considered.
options.explanation: A permeating solute can alter the effective osmotic gradient, so equal initial osmolarity does not guarantee stable cell volume.

options.text: Yes, provided diffusion uses no ATP.
options.explanation: Whether ATP is used does not determine tonicity; passive solute entry can still alter water balance.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: A plump endothelial venule lies in paracortical lymphoid tissue. Which route does it most directly support?

options.text: Afferent lymph entering the subcapsular sinus
options.explanation: Afferent lymphatics open into the subcapsular sinus. They are not the plump postcapillary blood venules described in the paracortex.

options.text: Lymph leaving through an epithelial crypt
options.explanation: A palatine tonsillar crypt is continuous with mucosal epithelium; it is not a lymph-node efferent passage.

options.text: Lymphocyte entry from blood into the node
options.explanation: An HEV is a specialised blood vessel. It is separate from the afferent lymphatic route.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: A medullary field contains cellular strands separated by lymph spaces. Which pairing fits?

options.text: A germinal centre and its epithelial crypt
options.explanation: A germinal centre is a region within a lymphoid follicle; a crypt is a mucosal invagination. That pairing does not describe medullary strands and intervening sinuses.

options.text: White pulp and a central arteriole
options.explanation: White pulp has an arterial relationship in spleen. The described lymph spaces and medullary cords fit node organisation.

options.text: Cellular medullary cords and intervening sinuses
options.explanation: Cords are tissue; the intervening medullary sinuses carry lymph.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: One pale centre occurs within a darker lymphoid nodule. What additional evidence is needed to identify the organ?

options.text: Its colour alone determines the germ layer
options.explanation: Stain colour describes contrast in the processed section, not developmental lineage. Germ-layer claims require developmental evidence.

options.text: Its position relative to capsule, mucosa and vessels
options.explanation: Follicles with germinal centres occur in several secondary lymphoid tissues.

options.text: No further evidence: it is always a lymph node
options.explanation: Germinal centres occur in nodes, splenic nodules and tonsillar lymphoid tissue. One follicle does not uniquely name the organ.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: A worksheet puts the paracortex between afferent lymphatics and medullary sinuses as though it were another sinus. What is the correction?

options.text: Make lymph enter through Hassall corpuscles
options.explanation: Hassall corpuscles are epithelial structures in thymic medulla. They are not lymph inflow openings.

options.text: Name the subcapsular/deeper sinus route and keep the paracortex as a tissue region
options.explanation: The cellular region and the named lymphatic passages must remain different entities.

options.text: Replace every sinus with a blood venule
options.explanation: Sinuses carrying lymph and venules carrying blood have distinct routes. Replacing one with the other removes the central distinction.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: An arteriole lies eccentrically relative to a lymphoid nodule surrounded by red pulp. Does eccentricity exclude spleen?

options.text: No; central describes a vascular association, not an invariant geometric centre
options.explanation: A two-dimensional section need not put a white-pulp arteriole at the centre of a nodule.

options.text: Yes; every central arteriole must be in the geometric centre
options.explanation: A section can intersect an arteriole away from the apparent centre of an associated nodule. The name does not impose that geometry.

options.text: Yes; any arteriole identifies lymph node
options.explanation: Arterioles occur in many organs. The surrounding white-pulp/red-pulp organisation matters more than the mere presence of an arteriole.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: Which assignment preserves the splenic compartments?

options.text: White pulp: lymphoid organisation; red pulp: cords and blood sinusoids
options.explanation: White pulp has lymphoid organisation; red pulp contains cellular cords and blood sinusoids.

options.text: White pulp: blood-only sinusoids; red pulp: T-cell follicles
options.explanation: This reverses the defining relationship. White pulp is the lymphoid component; red pulp includes blood-rich cords and sinusoids.

options.text: White pulp: thymic medulla; red pulp: tonsillar crypts
options.explanation: Cortex/medulla in thymus and crypts in tonsil are different arrangements. They cannot be substituted for splenic pulp compartments.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: A pale region within a lobular lymphoid organ contains concentric epithelial structures. Which comparison is strongest?

options.text: A tonsillar crypt because both are pale
options.explanation: A crypt is an epithelial-lined invagination continuous with a surface, not a concentric medullary epithelial corpuscle.

options.text: Thymic medulla with Hassall corpuscles rather than a lymph-node germinal centre
options.explanation: The epithelial corpuscles and lobular organisation support thymus.

options.text: A germinal centre because every pale lymphoid area is one
options.explanation: Paleness is shared by different structures. Concentric epithelial corpuscles within a lobular medulla support thymus rather than a follicular germinal centre.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: A lymphoid aggregate lies beneath an invaginated stratified squamous mucosal surface. What distinguishes a crypt from a node sinus?

options.text: Continuity with an epithelial-lined surface
options.explanation: Surface continuity is positive evidence; a subcapsular sinus lies beneath a connective-tissue capsule.

options.text: The pale colour of the space alone
options.explanation: Both genuine lumina and processing spaces may be pale. Demonstrating a lining and its continuity is stronger than colour.

options.text: The presence of any nearby lymphocyte
options.explanation: Lymphocytes occur in many locations. Their presence alone does not establish what bounds a space.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: Human third-pouch epithelial origin is established in a developmental study. What does this establish about thymocytes?

options.text: Thymocytes and splenic cords must have identical origins
options.explanation: Adult functional grouping as lymphoid organs does not imply identical developmental origins for every supporting cell population.

options.text: Their origin remains a separate haematopoietic lineage question
options.explanation: The adult organ contains populations with different developmental histories.

options.text: Every thymocyte must be an endodermal epithelial cell
options.explanation: The finding concerns epithelial cells, not every cell in the organ. Thymocytes belong to the haematopoietic population.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: An H&E section shows a follicle beside a sinus. Which claim needs a different kind of observation?

options.text: The presence of a lymphoid aggregate in the section
options.explanation: A visible lymphoid aggregate is a structural observation available in the displayed section; it does not require a time-resolved transport experiment.

options.text: The location of a capsule in the displayed section
options.explanation: A visible capsule can be located in a still section. That observation is different from measuring an antigen trajectory.

options.text: The time-dependent route taken by a labelled antigen
options.explanation: The conduit study used experimental imaging; a static section is not a trajectory measurement.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Identification and experimental reasoning
questions.prompt: A human embryology paper reports gene-expression localisation at ages measured after fertilisation. Which is the best way to use it in a developmental explanation?

options.text: Convert the localisation into proof that every adult thymic cell has the same origin.
options.explanation: An organ contains several cell populations; spatial expression is not universal lineage proof.

options.text: Label the reported ages as obstetric gestational weeks without adjustment.
options.explanation: The age convention differs; preserve the paper’s declared convention.

options.text: State the sampled stage, age convention and measured marker, then separate observation from inference.
options.explanation: This retains the experimental scope without treating expression localisation as human lineage tracing.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Preparation and stain reasoning
questions.prompt: A pink bundle is seen in H&E. What most improves a tendon-versus-smooth-muscle decision?

options.text: Assume pink means muscle
options.explanation: Eosinophilia is shared by many proteins, including collagen and muscle components. Pink colour alone does not establish muscle.

options.text: Assume absent striations means tendon
options.explanation: Smooth muscle lacks sarcomeric striations and section orientation can hide striations of striated muscle. Absence alone does not establish tendon.

options.text: Cell density, nuclear pattern and extracellular-fibre organisation
options.explanation: Both may be pink. Positive architectural features are needed.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Preparation and stain reasoning
questions.prompt: What does basophilic most directly describe here?

options.text: A measured intracellular alkaline pH
options.explanation: Stain affinity is not a calibrated pH measurement. Fixation, dye chemistry and the stained component influence the appearance.

options.text: A proof of high mitotic activity
options.explanation: A basophilic region can reflect nucleic-acid-rich material. It is not itself a mitotic index or direct activity measurement.

options.text: A staining affinity under the preparation conditions
options.explanation: The term describes dye affinity; it is not a pH or activity assay.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Preparation and stain reasoning
questions.prompt: A narrow structure lies outside the chosen section plane. Can changing H&E to trichrome guarantee it appears?

options.text: Yes; collagen colour determines the section plane
options.explanation: Collagen colour depends on the stain method. It cannot determine or change the orientation of the physical cut.

options.text: No; dye choice cannot recover a structure not intersected
options.explanation: Orientation and chemical contrast solve different problems.

options.text: Yes; all special stains reconstruct three dimensions
options.explanation: Special stains change chemical contrast. They do not reconstruct a missing section plane or add an uncut structure to the specimen.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Preparation and stain reasoning
questions.prompt: A routine paraffin section lacks visible lipid droplets. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Processing may have removed lipid; review the method before inferring biological absence
options.explanation: Preparation can change retained components; a method suited to lipid is a separate decision.

options.text: The original living tissue contained no lipid
options.explanation: Solvent processing can remove lipid that was present in the living tissue. Non-visibility after processing cannot alone establish its original absence.

options.text: The absent lipid proves the tissue is nervous
options.explanation: Many tissue types contain lipid, and processing effects are not specific to nervous tissue. Organ identification still needs architecture.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Preparation and stain reasoning
questions.prompt: PAS positivity alone is observed. What remains unresolved?

options.text: Which PAS-reactive component accounts for the signal in its anatomical context
options.explanation: Several carbohydrate-rich components can contribute; controls and context are required.

options.text: The signal must uniquely identify glycogen
options.explanation: PAS can highlight several carbohydrate-rich components. Distinguishing a glycogen contribution requires additional method/context, such as a suitable diastase comparison.

options.text: The signal proves a specific patient diagnosis
options.explanation: A histochemical signal alone lacks the anatomical, assay and clinical evidence needed for a specific diagnosis.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Preparation and stain reasoning
questions.prompt: A sharply dark doubled region follows a crease across otherwise intact tissue. What should be considered first?

options.text: A proven increase in cell production
options.explanation: Darkness in a folded section is not a direct measure of cell proliferation. The preparation alternative must be examined.

options.text: A fold and superposition of tissue, checked against adjacent regions
options.explanation: A preparation artefact is a plausible alternative, not a diagnosis.

options.text: A new tissue family defined by darkness
options.explanation: A darker crease can reflect superposed tissue. Tissue families are defined by organisation, not an arbitrary dark region.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Preparation and stain reasoning
questions.prompt: An antibody-stained section is positive, while an otherwise identical section processed without primary antibody is unstained. Which claim remains unresolved?

options.text: Whether the protocol used a primary antibody in the test section.
options.explanation: The stated protocol explicitly includes the primary antibody in the test section.

options.text: Whether the primary antibody binds the intended target in this tissue.
options.explanation: Omission removes the primary antibody and therefore cannot test its unintended binding. Target-specific validation requires additional evidence.

options.text: Whether visible staining occurred in the omission control.
options.explanation: The observation explicitly says that the omission control was unstained.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Preparation and stain reasoning
questions.prompt: The test section and an expected-positive anatomical control are both unstained. Which conclusion is justified first?

options.text: The negative test is not securely interpretable until control failure is investigated.
options.explanation: A failed expected-positive control removes evidence that the assay could detect the target under the run conditions.

options.text: The target must be absent from the test tissue.
options.explanation: Assay failure is an alternative to biological absence, so the negative result cannot establish absence.

options.text: The failed control proves the target is present in the test tissue.
options.explanation: Control failure does not prove the opposite biological result either.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Structure, development and evidence
questions.prompt: A parallel tubular bundle lies between regions containing renal corpuscles. Which interpretation fits the whole field?

options.text: A medullary ray within cortex.
options.explanation: Neighbouring corpuscles establish cortical context; a ray contains straight profiles within that cortex.

options.text: Medulla, because every straight tubule is medullary.
options.explanation: Straight tubules also occur in cortical rays.

options.text: A renal corpuscle cut longitudinally.
options.explanation: A corpuscle contains a capillary tuft and capsule, not a bundle of parallel epithelial tubes.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Structure, development and evidence
questions.prompt: A student traces filtrate from capsular space into the efferent arteriole. Where should that route go instead?

options.text: Directly into the renal pelvis.
options.explanation: Tubular processing occurs between filtration and the collecting-system outlet.

options.text: Through the urinary pole into the proximal tubule.
options.explanation: The urinary pole connects capsular space with tubular lumen.

options.text: Through the vascular pole into a venule.

options.explanation: Correct. This is remodeling of a spermatid, distinct from the divisions that produced it.

options.text: The first meiotic division.
options.explanation: Meiosis I concerns chromosome segregation and precedes the haploid spermatid stage described.

options.text: Spermiation.
options.explanation: Spermiation is release into the lumen; the prompt describes preceding differentiation.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Define the interval first
questions.prompt: One report describes recurrence of a seminiferous epithelial cell association; another describes progression through the full sperm-producing sequence. What must be compared before treating their durations as contradictory?

options.text: The anatomical organ alone; intervals measured in the same testis must be equivalent.
options.explanation: The same organ supports several overlapping processes with different start and end events.

options.text: The defined start and end events, species, sampling method and whether duct transit is included.
options.explanation: Correct. A recurring epithelial association, full germ-cell development and downstream transit are distinct intervals. Numerical disagreement still needs source evaluation.

options.text: The sperm concentration alone; it directly converts one developmental interval into the other.
options.explanation: Concentration depends on additional production, transport and sampling factors and does not define the measured interval.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Location before function
questions.prompt: A student labels an interstitial steroid-producing cell as the cell forming the seminiferous junctional barrier. Which correction is most useful?

options.text: All interstitial cells form the same barrier.
options.explanation: The barrier at issue is formed between epithelial Sertoli cells, not every interstitial cell.

options.text: The barrier must instead lie at the luminal tip of each sperm.
options.explanation: Sperm are not the neighboring epithelial cells forming this junctional division.

options.text: Separate Leydig steroid production in interstitium from Sertoli junctions within the seminiferous epithelium.
options.explanation: Correct. The two populations occupy different compartments and serve different functions.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Place the sealing interface
questions.prompt: Which schematic best locates the junctional blood–testis barrier?

options.text: A junctional connection between neighboring Sertoli cells dividing basal and adluminal epithelial compartments.
options.explanation: Correct. This is the relevant epithelial division; the nearby vessel is a separate landmark.

options.text: A tight seal drawn only between testicular vascular endothelial cells.
options.explanation: That substitutes a vascular location for the Sertoli junctional barrier being taught.

options.text: The entire interstitial region shaded as a single impermeable wall.
options.explanation: Interstitial tissue is a compartment, not the specific epithelial junctional seal.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Choose the functional assay
questions.prompt: H&E shows an apparently continuous seminiferous boundary. Which additional evidence most directly addresses access by a specified test substance?

options.text: A larger number of identical H&E images without a tracer.
options.explanation: More morphology improves sampling but does not directly test passage of the substance.

options.text: A controlled tracer-distribution experiment with the substance, tissue conditions and timing defined.
options.explanation: Correct. It tests access under specified conditions, while retaining limits of the assay.

options.text: Detection of any junction-associated transcript in a whole-tissue sample.
options.explanation: A transcript measurement does not directly establish localization or functional permeability.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Association versus requirement
questions.prompt: A barrier-defective mouse shows autoantibodies. Removing mature adaptive lymphocytes does not restore spermatogenesis. Which interpretation fits the tested result?

options.text: Autoantibody staining alone proves that adaptive immunity caused the reproductive failure.
options.explanation: The failure to rescue does not support that simple requirement claim.

options.text: The experiment proves that immunity has no role in any reproductive disorder.
options.explanation: That generalization exceeds one intervention and model.

options.text: The associated immune response is insufficient evidence that adaptive immunity is required for this phenotype in this model.
options.explanation: Correct. The perturbation addresses causal requirement more directly than association alone.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Count biological replication
questions.prompt: A study collects ten fields from each of three independently studied mice. What should remain explicit when reporting replication?

options.text: There are three biological animals, with fields nested within animals.
options.explanation: Correct. The sampling hierarchy matters; fields are not automatically independent animals.

options.text: There are thirty independent mice because each field supplies a measurement.
options.explanation: That confuses observations within an animal with biological replication.

options.text: There is only one observation because all fields concern the same organ type.
options.explanation: Common organ identity does not erase the independent animals or the nested observations.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Profiles and objects
questions.prompt: Several similar duct profiles appear in one section of a highly coiled epididymal duct. Which follow-up best addresses whether two profiles are continuous?

options.text: Assign one duct to each closed outline, then add the outlines across adjacent sections.
options.explanation: That counts intersections and risks counting the same coiled structure repeatedly.

options.text: Trace the profiles through registered serial sections or another suitable three-dimensional reconstruction.
options.explanation: Correct. Following continuity addresses the anatomical relationship that a single section cannot establish.

options.text: Match the two luminal diameters; equal diameters establish that the profiles are continuous.
options.explanation: Diameter similarity does not establish continuity and is affected by section angle and local variation.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Compare surface specializations
questions.prompt: A student assumes that the long apical projections of epididymal principal cells propel sperm by beating. Which structural explanation corrects that inference?

options.text: They are motile cilia, so their appearance establishes an active ciliary transport mechanism.
options.explanation: This assigns the motile-cilium mechanism to the wrong specialization; a static section also cannot show beating.

options.text: They are solitary primary cilia, so each visible fringe represents one sensory axoneme.
options.explanation: The long epididymal surface fringe is not explained as a single primary cilium on each cell.

options.text: They are elongated microvilli called stereocilia; their presence does not establish ciliary beating.
options.explanation: Correct. Similar length or a cilia-like name does not make these projections motile cilia. Duct transport needs its own mechanism and evidence.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Do not identify from one wavy line
questions.prompt: An unknown duct has an uneven luminal contour. Which observation would strengthen an efferent-ductule interpretation?

options.text: A suitable view demonstrating alternating cell heights and ciliated/nonciliated epithelial populations.
options.explanation: Correct. It adds cell-level evidence to a contour that could otherwise reflect folds or section angle.

options.text: A conclusion based only on the contour, regardless of cells or region.
options.explanation: A wavy outline is not exclusive to one duct.

options.text: Any adjacent connective tissue, even without a visible lining.
options.explanation: Connective tissue accompanies many structures and is not sufficiently discriminatory.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Duct or vessel in spermatic cord
questions.prompt: A thick-walled profile appears in spermatic cord. Which next step best separates a reproductive duct from a muscular vessel?

options.text: Use wall thickness alone.
options.explanation: Both can have substantial muscular walls.

options.text: Compare the lining, mucosal folds, contents and surrounding context.
options.explanation: Correct. These features test the structural alternatives rather than assuming one from thickness.

options.text: Treat every circular lumen in spermatic cord as ductus deferens.
options.explanation: The cord also contains vessels and other components.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: One folded surface or many glands
questions.prompt: A specimen shows a labyrinth of epithelial-lined spaces. Which comparison best helps distinguish seminal vesicle from prostate?

options.text: Choose the organ with the darker overall stain.
options.explanation: Stain intensity depends on preparation and is not the key architectural distinction.

options.text: Count lumina and call every lumen an independent gland.
options.explanation: A folded surface can create many apparently separate spaces in section.

options.text: Trace mucosal folds and compare them with glandular profiles distributed through fibromuscular stroma.
options.explanation: Correct. This tests the underlying three-dimensional organization.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: What an atlas cannot prove alone
questions.prompt: A gonadal atlas measures marker expression and groups cells by transcriptional similarity. Which additional claim is not established by that expression analysis alone?

options.text: A particular cell state is the direct ancestor of another and lies beside it in the intact gonad.
options.explanation: Correct. Ancestry and physical position require evidence beyond similarity; spatial assays address location, while lineage inference needs separate support.

options.text: The measured expression profiles can be compared to describe molecular differences between sampled states.
options.explanation: That is within the purpose of the expression measurements, provided technical and sampling limitations are retained.

options.text: The reported marker measurements can help annotate the sampled clusters.
options.explanation: Marker-based annotation is possible, but annotation alone should not be promoted to direct lineage or spatial proof.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Keep the developmental clock attached
questions.prompt: A mouse perturbation is reported at a particular embryonic day. Which use in a human embryology lesson is best?

options.text: Relabel that day as the same numbered human week.
options.explanation: Cross-species stages are not interchangeable by number.

options.text: Retain species, stage and assay, and verify any human comparison separately.
options.explanation: Correct. This preserves the experimental context and prevents an unsupported human timetable.

options.text: Omit the organism because the gene name is shared.
options.explanation: Shared names do not ensure identical timing, expression or outcome.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Initiation versus maintenance
questions.prompt: An altered mouse gonad initially expresses SOX9 but later loses the signal and fails to organize normal cords. Which distinction matters most?

options.text: Initial marker detection is the same outcome as stable organ differentiation.
options.explanation: The later observations directly show why these outcomes must be separated.

options.text: A later negative result makes the earlier observation impossible.
options.explanation: A developmental state can change over time.

options.text: Initiating expression, maintaining the program and forming tissue architecture are distinct outcomes.
options.explanation: Correct. The temporal sequence supports this more precise account.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Read a gain-of-function design
questions.prompt: Adding a tested Sry genomic fragment leads to testicular development in XX mice. Which claim is directly supported by that design?

options.text: The tested fragment can be sufficient for the observed developmental outcome in that context.
options.explanation: Correct. The addition tests a sufficiency claim under the specified conditions.

options.text: Every sequence in the fragment is individually necessary for normal development.
options.explanation: Necessity of individual elements requires other experiments.

options.text: Normal fertility and dosage are guaranteed in every resulting animal.
options.explanation: Those outcomes are not established by the stated developmental observation.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Separate production and delivery
questions.prompt: In a specified experimental mouse model, sperm are present but abnormal retained reproductive structures interfere with delivery. What does this demonstrate?

options.text: Finding sperm proves the entire tract is normally patterned.
options.explanation: The structural and delivery findings contradict that inference.

options.text: Gamete production, duct pattern and reproductive function must be assessed separately.
options.explanation: Correct. They are connected but distinct outcomes.

options.text: Any abnormal duct pattern proves that germ cells cannot complete differentiation.
options.explanation: The stated observations include sperm, so that conclusion is unsupported.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Name the anatomical precursor precisely
questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes efferent ductules from the principal mesonephric duct derivatives?

options.text: Every epithelium and stromal component arises from the same duct segment.
options.explanation: This collapses separate epithelial sources and surrounding tissues.

options.text: Efferent ductules arise from the adult epididymal duct after puberty.
options.explanation: That replaces an embryological contribution with an unsupported later origin.

options.text: Selected mesonephric tubules contribute to efferent ductules, while the mesonephric duct contributes to the epididymal/deferent route.
options.explanation: Correct. Tubules and the duct are distinct precursors.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Read an early prostate bud
questions.prompt: Early prostate epithelium can co-express markers later associated with basal and luminal populations. What is the best interpretation of such an early bud?

options.text: Early co-expression does not establish mature basal/luminal compartments; compare the marker pattern with canalization and tissue position.
options.explanation: Correct. Differentiation includes changing marker restriction and organization. A solid bud should not be assigned the compartment structure of a mature gland.

options.text: Every co-expressing cell must already be a fully differentiated adult secretory cell.
options.explanation: A marker combination in an early developmental state does not establish adult secretory specialization.

options.text: The markers prove two mature layers are present even if no lumen or separate layers can be demonstrated.
options.explanation: This makes anatomical organization follow from marker names rather than observing the developing tissue.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Interpret a xenograft
questions.prompt: Human fetal tissue develops under an experimental host and defined hormone exposure. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: The experiment gives an exact normal timetable for every human fetus.
options.explanation: The experimental environment and staging uncertainty prevent that universal inference.

options.text: It measures a response under the specified graft and exposure conditions.
options.explanation: Correct. The model and intervention remain part of the interpretation.

options.text: Any observed differentiation must have occurred before grafting.
options.explanation: That would require evidence; the experiment is intended to examine developmental response.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: A gap after processing
questions.prompt: An apparent cleft separates tissue elements in a prepared section. What is the most defensible next step?

options.text: Declare it a normal anatomical channel solely because it is pale.
options.explanation: A pale gap can reflect preparation or sectioning effects.

options.text: Exclude every biological interpretation without inspecting further evidence.
options.explanation: Artifact is a possibility to investigate, not an automatic conclusion.

options.text: Assess preparation, neighboring sections and anatomical context before distinguishing a real space from processing separation.
options.explanation: Correct. This tests the alternative explanations rather than choosing from appearance alone.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Chromosome sets and DNA amount
questions.prompt: A germ cell has completed meiosis I but has not entered meiosis II. For the usual human chromosome complement, which description is correct?

options.text: 23 chromosomes, each still containing two sister chromatids; n, 2C.
options.explanation: Meiosis I separates homologues. The remaining chromosomes retain paired chromatids until meiosis II.

options.text: 46 chromosomes with unreplicated DNA; 2n, 2C.
options.explanation: This confuses the post-meiosis-I cell with a diploid cell before DNA replication.

options.text: 23 single-chromatid chromosomes; n, 1C.
options.explanation: This is the standard product after meiosis II, not the secondary spermatocyte before that division.

options.text: 46 two-chromatid chromosomes; 2n, 4C.
options.explanation: That describes the replicated primary spermatocyte before the reduction division.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Compaction is not another reduction division
questions.prompt: A series of spermatids shows progressively smaller, denser nuclei. Which explanation connects the appearance with the relevant process without overclaiming what H&E demonstrates?

options.text: A dense nucleus proves that epididymal maturation has been completed.
options.explanation: The change can occur within seminiferous epithelium before epididymal passage.

options.text: Chromatin is being repackaged during spermiogenesis; a specific protein claim needs a targeted assay.
options.explanation: Compaction is part of differentiation. H&E appearance alone does not identify transition proteins or protamines.

options.text: Each smaller nucleus must have lost another complete chromosome set.
options.explanation: Nuclear condensation does not imply successive reduction divisions or further loss of chromosome sets.

options.text: The dark colour directly identifies protamine 1 concentration.
options.explanation: H&E is not a protamine-specific quantitative assay.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Follow the hormone to its receiving cell
questions.prompt: An original teaching diagram shows LH reaching an interstitial cell and FSH reaching a seminiferous supporting cell. Which labels and downstream relationship fit?

options.text: LH and FSH both act only on the epididymal lumen.
options.explanation: The diagram concerns endocrine targets within testicular tissue, not hormones acting only within duct contents.

options.text: Detectable testosterone guarantees that every target cell responds normally.
options.explanation: A ligand concentration does not establish receptor function in the receiving cell.

options.text: LH → Leydig cell; FSH → Sertoli cell; Leydig-derived testosterone can also act on androgen-responsive Sertoli cells.
options.explanation: This distinguishes two pituitary targets and the separate local androgen response.

options.text: LH → spermatid; FSH → Leydig cell; sperm make the junctional barrier.
options.explanation: These targets and the barrier-forming cell identity are incorrect.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Separate a marker from demonstrated competence
questions.prompt: In a mouse Sertoli-cell androgen-receptor knockout, surviving spermatocytes display several prophase markers but respond poorly in the tested induction of meiotic division. Which inference is supported?

options.text: The measured marker proves that meiosis and fertility are normal.
options.explanation: A marker does not demonstrate completion of division or fertility.

options.text: No germ cell in the animal can have entered meiotic prophase.
options.explanation: This contradicts the stated observation of surviving prophase cells.

options.text: The same phenotype identifies one specific diagnosis in a human biopsy.
options.explanation: A conditional mouse experiment does not supply that individual clinical inference.

options.text: Early cytological features and competence for the later division are distinct; supporting-cell signalling can affect germ-cell progression.
options.explanation: The model changes a somatic supporting-cell receptor and measures several non-equivalent germ-cell readouts.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Reason through a moving compartment boundary
questions.prompt: A fixed mouse preparation shows junction-associated boundaries on both sides of transiting spermatocytes. Which model best accommodates the observation?

options.text: An intermediate compartment can form as new basal contacts develop before removal of the older adluminal boundary.
options.explanation: Coexisting boundaries support staged compartment rearrangement without assuming unrestricted opening of the whole epithelium.

options.text: The entire seminiferous epithelium must become completely open at once.
options.explanation: That is not required by a pattern with boundaries on both sides.

options.text: The image is a continuous movie that directly measures every transport step.
options.explanation: A reconstruction from fixed samples does not provide continuous live temporal measurements.

options.text: The endothelial capillary wall alone explains the observed epithelial compartments.
options.explanation: The described boundaries are between Sertoli cells within the seminiferous epithelium.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Compare the supporting tissue
questions.prompt: Two original specimen descriptions both mention secretory epithelium. One emphasizes complex mucosal folds with stromal cores; the other emphasizes glands distributed through substantial fibromuscular stroma. Which comparison is most useful?

options.text: Each apparently separate space is necessarily a separate gland.
options.explanation: A section through folded connected surfaces can generate apparently isolated spaces.

options.text: The first favours seminal-vesicle architecture; the second favours prostate, with cell-level and contextual confirmation.
options.explanation: The relation of epithelium, lumen and supporting tissue is more discriminating than a shared secretory role.

options.text: Both must be seminal vesicle because secretion is present.
options.explanation: Several reproductive glands secrete; secretion alone does not identify the organ.

options.text: Absence of a luminal concretion excludes prostate.
options.explanation: Concretions need not be visible in every prostatic field.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Include mesenchyme in a developmental explanation
questions.prompt: A mouse study alters androgen-receptor activity in mesenchymal cells and reports abnormal duct morphology and smooth-muscle differentiation. The in-vivo and explant patterns differ. Which explanation is best?

options.text: The explant result proves an identical bilateral outcome in every intact embryo.
options.explanation: The stem explicitly distinguishes those settings.

options.text: The result establishes the direction of every proliferation measurement without checking the paper.
options.explanation: That exceeds the described morphological findings; conflicting proliferation wording remains excluded.

options.text: Epithelial organization depends on surrounding tissue interactions, and experimental context can change the outcome.
options.explanation: Epithelial origin, mesenchymal response and the conditions of the experiment are separate parts of the explanation.

options.text: Only the epithelial ancestral duct matters; its surroundings are irrelevant.
options.explanation: The reported intervention and phenotype specifically implicate surrounding mesenchyme.

questions.subject: histology
questions.title: Choose a method for the question
questions.prompt: A student wants to distinguish collagen-rich stroma from muscle in one specimen and test a specific protein’s location in another. Which plan matches the questions?

options.text: Use H&E colour alone as an exact measurement of the target protein.
options.explanation: General histological contrast is not a specific quantitative protein assay.

options.text: Treat any colour difference between slides as proof of a biological difference.
options.explanation: Preparation, staining and imaging can change contrast independently of biology.

options.text: Assume that RNA signal, protein localization and barrier permeability are interchangeable readouts.
options.explanation: Transcript, protein and transport measurements answer different questions.

options.text: Use an appropriate connective-tissue stain for structural contrast and a separately controlled protein-localization assay.
options.explanation: These methods address different targets; retain the staining protocol, controls and tissue context.

questions.title: Recover the missing context
questions.prompt: A high-power breast field shows an epithelial ring and a lumen, but the student cannot decide whether it belongs to a lobular group or a larger conducting structure. Which next step most directly addresses that uncertainty?

options.text: Inspect a lower-power field that includes neighboring epithelial units and stroma.
options.explanation: Architecture supplies the relationship missing from the isolated cellular view.

options.text: Increase magnification until individual nuclear chromatin is easier to see.
options.explanation: Better nuclear detail does not recover the missing relationship to neighboring units.

options.text: Classify the profile from its lumen diameter alone.
options.explanation: Diameter varies with section plane and context; it does not independently establish branch level or function.

options.text: Use the darkest nucleus to identify the whole gland.
options.explanation: A single nuclear appearance is not an organ-level architectural criterion.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Interpret peripheral nuclei
questions.prompt: In an H&E mammary field, several small dark nuclei lie near the outside of an epithelial profile. Which conclusion is best supported without additional staining?

options.text: They have demonstrated contractile function because of their position.
options.explanation: A fixed nuclear position does not measure contraction.

options.text: Their peripheral position is visible, but their exact phenotype remains unconfirmed.
options.explanation: Position is directly observable; specific myoepithelial identity may require additional localization and marker evidence.

options.text: They must all be stromal fibroblasts because they are dark.
options.explanation: Darkness does not distinguish all basal epithelial and stromal cell types.

options.text: They prove that the profile has no basal epithelial component.
options.explanation: The field does not support that exclusion, and section geometry may obscure boundaries.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Control a comparison
questions.prompt: A learner compares postmenopausal human H&E with a lactating osmium preparation and attributes every dark region in the second slide to lactation. What is the most important design problem?

options.text: Different stains always make tissue comparisons impossible.
options.explanation: Comparisons remain useful if their distinct readouts and limits are acknowledged.

options.text: The older specimen cannot contain epithelial tissue.
options.explanation: Age context does not justify that absolute conclusion.

options.text: Functional state and preparation changed together, so their contributions are confounded.
options.explanation: The stain changes what is emphasized; a matched preparation helps isolate the biological comparison.

options.text: The darkest areas necessarily represent the greatest number of cells.
options.explanation: Osmium lipid staining is not a cell-count assay.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Explain an edge pattern
questions.prompt: In the documented Columbia osmium example, dark staining is strongest near the specimen edge. Which explanation should be considered before proposing a universal biological lipid gradient?

options.text: All mammary secretory cells migrate to the edge before releasing lipid.
options.explanation: That migration claim is not established by the preparation or its staining pattern.

options.text: The center must contain only protein and no lipid.
options.explanation: Weak staining can reflect preparation limits and does not prove absence of lipid.

options.text: The edge is a calibrated measure of milk production rate.
options.explanation: Staining intensity in a fixed preparation is not a production-rate measurement.

options.text: Limited reagent penetration through this specimen.
options.explanation: The source specifically documents a penetration limitation; the pattern need not represent an organ-wide biological gradient.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Choose a secretory model
questions.prompt: A teaching diagram sends protein vesicles and cytoplasmic lipid droplets through one identical release step. Which revision best represents the distinction supported by the reviewed sources?

options.text: Show vesicular protein exocytosis and lipid-droplet envelopment/budding as separate routes.
options.explanation: Cargo and membrane behavior differ; one label for the whole gland loses that distinction.

options.text: Show both cargo types leaving only when the entire cell disintegrates.
options.explanation: That substitutes whole-cell destruction for the described secretory mechanisms.

options.text: Show protein leaving without vesicles because lipid uses membrane.
options.explanation: The routes can both involve membrane while doing so in different ways.

options.text: Remove all membrane boundaries because H&E cannot resolve the events.
options.explanation: A sourced conceptual model can explain events beyond H&E resolution if it is clearly distinguished from the image.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Identify the measured event
questions.prompt: A live mouse mammary sequence shows two visible lipid droplets joining into one larger droplet. Which statement is most directly supported by that observation?

options.text: The cell doubled its lipid synthesis rate at that instant.
options.explanation: An increase in droplet size through fusion does not establish a synthesis-rate change.

options.text: The observed droplets underwent a fusion event in the imaged preparation.
options.explanation: The sequence directly follows merging; it does not by itself quantify synthesis or secretion.

options.text: The larger droplet has already been released into the lumen.
options.explanation: Fusion inside the observed cell is a different event from release.

options.text: Every human mammary droplet follows the same time course.
options.explanation: The observation is bounded by species, preparation and sampled particles.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Separate sampling levels
questions.prompt: A kinetic study tracks 300 droplets in three mice. Which description preserves the sampling hierarchy?

options.text: The biological sample size is automatically 300 independent mice.
options.explanation: The tracked objects and the animals are different experimental units.

options.text: Only three droplets can be included in any analysis.
options.explanation: Hierarchical data can contain many within-animal observations; analysis must respect dependence.

options.text: There are many droplet observations nested within three animals.
options.explanation: Droplets share animal-level conditions; the count does not create 300 independent animals.

options.text: The number of animals is irrelevant once images are quantitative.
options.explanation: Quantification does not remove clustering or biological variation.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Recognize an invisible population
questions.prompt: An imaging method cannot resolve the smallest lipid droplets. Which interpretation of the tracked-particle results is strongest?

options.text: They prove that smaller droplets do not exist.
options.explanation: Failure to resolve a structure is not evidence of biological absence.

options.text: They require all observed motion to be discarded.
options.explanation: A resolution boundary limits scope without nullifying directly observed events.

options.text: They establish an exact whole-gland particle census.
options.explanation: The method excludes a population and samples selected fields.

options.text: They characterize the observable droplets under the stated preparation and resolution.
options.explanation: The unobserved small-particle population is not automatically represented by tracked larger particles.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Read an early human bud
questions.prompt: An abstract describes solid early human mammary epithelial ingrowth next to differentiating mesenchyme, with no lumen in the sampled material. Which conclusion stays within that observation?

options.text: The sampled early structure differs from a later lumen-containing glandular profile.
options.explanation: This is a structural comparison; it does not require an unreviewed timetable or causal pathway.

options.text: A specific signaling ligand has been shown to cause the ingrowth.
options.explanation: Spatial association alone does not establish a molecular cause.

options.text: No human mammary structure can ever develop a lumen.
options.explanation: The finding concerns the sampled early material, not every subsequent stage.

options.text: Mouse embryonic dates can be assigned directly to this human series.
options.explanation: Species and developmental timing conventions cannot be equated that way.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Interpret a marker panel
questions.prompt: Fetal basal cells express part of a myoepithelial marker panel. Which additional question is not answered by that marker finding alone?

options.text: Whether the tested markers produced detectable staining in the sampled cells.
options.explanation: That is the direct observation described by the result, assuming valid controls.

options.text: Whether those cells demonstrate mature contractile function.
options.explanation: Phenotypic staining and functional behavior are distinct readouts.

options.text: Whether the stained cells occupy a reported basal position in the section.
options.explanation: Localization can be assessed in the same histological preparation.

options.text: Whether the observed panel differs from complete absence of its staining.
options.explanation: A validated partial-positive pattern supplies that limited distinction.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Distinguish marker from lineage
questions.prompt: An embryonic cell expresses both basal-associated and luminal-associated markers. Which experiment most directly tests whether its descendants populate both compartments?

options.text: Repeat a single-time-point stain with a brighter fluorophore.
options.explanation: That improves detection but does not follow descendants through time.

options.text: Measure only the cell diameter on an adjacent section.
options.explanation: Size does not establish the developmental fate of progeny.

options.text: Induce a suitably sparse heritable label and classify descendants after a defined chase.
options.explanation: The design connects a labeling event with later progeny while requiring controls for targeting and clonality.

options.text: Assume that every double-positive cell must be permanently bipotent.
options.explanation: Marker coexpression alone does not prove the future lineage outcome.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Interpret a chance model
questions.prompt: Later Notch1-labeling outcomes are not statistically distinguishable from modeled chance mixtures. Which conclusion avoids overstatement?

options.text: Every cell in every mammary gland is conclusively incapable of bipotency.
options.explanation: A bounded failure to establish a signal does not prove that universal negative.

options.text: The early above-chance results must be false because later results differ.
options.explanation: Developmental stage and targeted populations can differ; one does not automatically invalidate the other.

options.text: The analysis proves all mixed labels come from one progenitor.
options.explanation: The chance model addresses the competing possibility of independent labeling.

options.text: This design did not establish above-chance bipotency for that labeled population under those conditions.
options.explanation: The conclusion retains targeting, power and model limits instead of asserting universal absence.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Compare lineage systems
questions.prompt: K14 and Notch1 induction experiments give different lineage distributions. What should be compared before proposing a contradiction?

options.text: Targeted cells, induction stage, labeling density, chase and clone-assignment method.
options.explanation: These features determine which population and outcome each experiment can test.

options.text: Only the color used for the reporter in the published figure.
options.explanation: Color display does not establish equivalent targeting or analysis.

options.text: Only the publication year, treating the newer result as automatically correct.
options.explanation: Recency alone does not adjudicate differences in experimental design.

options.text: The results should be averaged into a universal human switch date.
options.explanation: Different mouse designs do not generate a human timetable by averaging.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Bound a perturbation claim
questions.prompt: Constitutive Notch activation changes a lineage outcome in a targeted mouse population. Which interpretation best preserves the experiment's scope?

options.text: Every human progenitor normally experiences the same constitutive activation.
options.explanation: The intervention does not establish that normal physiological exposure.

questions.prompt: Secretory epithelium occupies a greater fraction of one field than in another. Which additional caution is appropriate?

options.text: The greater epithelial fraction proves that all connective tissue has disappeared.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Plan the next useful specimen
questions.prompt: A candidate H&E image has a clear lumen, epithelial lining and external stroma but no scale or functional-state metadata. Which addition most improves a beginner's organ-identification journey?

options.text: An exact hormonal-state label inferred solely from the image filename.
options.explanation: A filename does not provide independent biological verification.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Identify an organizational unit
questions.prompt: A section contains a cluster of small acinar profiles associated with a terminal duct and a shared local stromal environment. Which label describes this relationship most precisely?

options.text: Terminal duct–lobular unit

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Distinguish stromal scales
questions.prompt: A student labels a broad H&E-pink collagen bundle between lobules as the basement membrane of one acinus. What is the central error?

options.text: Assuming that connective tissue can stain pink

options.text: Using low power before high power
options.explanation: Beginning with architecture is appropriate; the interpretation of the structure is the error.

questions.subject: histology

questions.title: Map ligand access
questions.prompt: Polarized mouse mammary cells on a permeable support express prolactin receptor. Basal prolactin strongly activates STAT5, while apical prolactin has little effect. Which explanation fits the reviewed experiment?

options.explanation: Basal activation shows that downstream machinery is present.

options.text: The receptor is chiefly basolateral, so the ligand must reach that compartment

questions.subject: histology

questions.prompt: After transplantation into a hormonally competent mouse host, mutant mammary epithelium produces ducts but lacks normal functional secretory alveoli. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.explanation: A lumen is a structural observation and does not establish secretory function.

options.text: All transcripts are absent in every mutant cell

questions.subject: histology
